title: The Moral Mind(s) of Large Language Models
findings: The paper does not contain findings related to religion. Its analysis of the 'moral mind' of LLMs is based on a secular framework derived from economic theory and does not test for religious knowledge, bias, or reasoning.

measurement_description: The benchmark does not measure faith or religion. It measures the consistency of moral preferences in large language models across five dimensions of ethical reasoning (honesty vs. compassion, efficiency vs. moral agency, privacy vs. collective welfare, harm reduction, and liberty vs. common good) using tools from economic revealed preference theory.
